Fictional scene: Hana saw a puzzled face and nearly ended the conversation.

我说错了。
Wǒ shuō cuò le.
I said it wrong.

说 shuō = say; 错 cuò = wrong. The mistake didn’t have to end the exchange. A repair sentence gave her another turn.

Original mini-fable: Mouse argued all evening that a shadow was a monster. Moth moved the lantern. It was a coat.

让我看看。
Ràng wǒ kànkan.
Let me take a look.

看看 kànkan = take a look. A closer look did what a louder argument couldn’t.

source: Hanzi Threads approved Nov9 draft bank read earlier Nov7; fresh X-native adaptations; previous reservations preserved
